title: Reticle Inspection - Voids Detection on Zeta-388
subtitle: Final Inspection Quality Validation for 10nm Node Manufacturing
author: Dr. Amir Patel

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Zeta-388 system to detect and classify Voids defects during final inspection inspection at the 10nm technology node. The test is conducted at Milpitas Fab B to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 300mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Voids defects that are critical to yield at the 10nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Zeta-388 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Zeta-388
- Inspection Type: Reticle Inspection
- Target Defect: Voids
- Process Step: Final Inspection
- Wafer Size: 300mm
- Technology Node: 10nm
- Fab Location: Milpitas Fab B

This test case applies to all Zeta-388 systems deployed at Milpitas Fab B for final inspection monitoring in the 10nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Zeta-388
Software Version: v12.7.434
Recipe: RETICLE_INSPECTION_10nm_FINAL INSPECTION
Illumination Mode: Brightfield
Scan Speed: Low (187 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.25μm
Edge Exclusion: 3mm
Sampling Plan: Full wafer sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Zeta-388 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'Reticle Inspection' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Voids defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 10nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 84 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 90% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±2.6% for Reticle Inspection
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.95 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2025-06-10
Wafers Tested: 34
Total Defects Found: 1134
Defect Density: 160.43 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 5.9%
Capture Rate: 98.7%
Test Duration: 103 minutes
System Uptime: 97.7%

Result Classification: CONDITIONAL PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Zeta-388 demonstrated acceptable performance in detecting Voids at the 10nm node.

b) The capture rate exceeded the minimum threshold, confirming system readiness.

c) Nuisance rate exceeds the target threshold; recipe tuning is recommended.

d) Cross-correlation with the reference SEM confirmed classification accuracy.

e) The defect review station correlation was within specification.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Review edge-zone detection parameters for optimization.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Monitor performance over next 30 production days.
